key_insight: Hierarchical multipoint anchoring strengthens buried interfaces in inverted perovskite solar cells, improving efficiency and resistance to thermal cycling.
engineering_relevance: Engineering interfacial adhesion offers a route to reduce stress-driven device failure under realistic temperature fluctuations.
method: Pretreat transparent conductive oxides with a homometallic halide to guide ordered self-assembled monolayer formation.
Increase surface hydroxyl density to strengthen metal–oxygen coordination.
Use cooperative chloride-induced hydrogen bonding to reinforce interfacial anchoring.
evidence_signal: Devices achieved 27.3% efficiency (26.9% certified) and retained 94% of initial efficiency after 400 ISOS-T-3 temperature cycles between −40 and 85 °C.
watch_item: Thermal-cycle durability does not alone establish long-term field reliability or compatibility with large-area manufacturing.
paper_title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
